study_schedule.source_excerpt: protocolSection.descriptionModule.detailedDescription: "Omalizumab is administered subcutaneously every 4 weeks as an add-on therapy to the current approved treatment of adult CSU patients." "The treatment period is 28 weeks which is followed by an 8-week follow-up." "The study is divided into a 2-week screening period, a 28-week double-blind treatment phase with omalizumab or placebo-omalizumab, and an 8-week follow-up phase." -- The registry states phase durations but does not give week anchors for their boundaries, a total participation duration, or a per-visit schedule. The selected file contains narrative text rather than a full visit schedule table, so visit weeks are not inferred from outcome assessment time frames. The treatment is described as every 4 weeks as add-on therapy.

value.rationale: CT.gov results explicitly report rescue medication during the treatment period, including nsH1-antihistamine, clemastine, and corticosteroid rescue; corticosteroid categories include betamethasone, prednisolone, and prednisolone succinate. Participant flow also lists discontinuation for rescue medication after week 24. These results establish that rescue medication was used and identify the reported categories, but do not specify the clinical trigger, permission rules, or route; those rules are therefore left unasserted.
